items.sentence_raw: The disappointing results of many conventional road transport projects in Africa led some experts to rethink the strategy by which rural transport problems were to be tackled at the beginning of the 1980s.

items.sentence_raw: A request for help in improving the availability of transport within the remote Makete District of south-western Tanzania presented the opportunity to try a new approach.
items.explain: Q40: The passage starts by explaining why a new approach was needed and ends by showing Makete as a model for the future. The whole text describes the project's actions and results. Option **B** (*'describe how MIRTP was implemented and how successful it was'*) matches this. ***Option C is a trap*** because donkeys are just one small part, not the main aim.

items.sentence_raw: The concept of 'integrated rural transport' was adopted in the task of examining the transport needs of the rural households in the district.
The objective was to reduce the time and effort needed to obtain access to essential goods and services through an improved rural transport system.
The underlying assumption was that the time saved would be used instead for activities that would improve the social and economic development of the communities.
The Makete Integrated Rural Transport Project (MIRTP) started in 1985 with financial support from the Swiss Development Corporation and was co-ordinated with the help of the Tanzanian government.
When the project began, Makete District was virtually totally isolated during the rainy season.
items.explain: Q32: The question says the district was *'almost inaccessible'* in the rainy season. The passage uses the exact same idea, saying Makete was *'virtually totally isolated during the rainy season'*. **'Virtually totally isolated'** means **'almost inaccessible'**, so the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: The regional road was in such bad shape that access to the main towns was impossible for about three months of the year.
items.explain: Q39: The question asks about the isolation of Makete. The passage says the road was so bad that *'access to the main towns was impossible for about three months'*. This isolation was a problem before the roads were improved, but the ending says it *'was no longer a problem once the roads had been improved'*, which matches ending **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Road traffic was extremely rare within the district, and alternative means of transport were restricted to donkeys in the north of the district.
People relied primarily on the paths, which were slippery and dangerous during the rains.
Before solutions could be proposed, the problems had to be understood.
Little was known about the transport demands of the rural households, so Phase I, between December 1985 and December 1987, focused on research.
items.explain: Q31: The question says there were **'five phases'**, but the passage only lists *'Phase I'*, *'Phase II'*, and *'Phase III'*. ***Five is not three***, so the number in the statement is wrong. The text clearly names just these **three** stages of work. Therefore, the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: The socio-economic survey of more than 400 households in the district indicated that a household in Makete spent, on average, seven hours a day on transporting themselves and their goods, a figure which seemed extreme but which has also been obtained in surveys in other rural areas in Africa.
items.explain:
Q27: Students often confuse this section with just listing problems, but the key is that Phase I was about *finding out* what the problems were. The passage says a *'socio-economic survey'* found households spent *'seven hours a day'* on transport, and it lists facts like *'95% was on foot'*. This is all about **identifying** the main issues, so the heading is **ii**.

Q33: The question says the survey was about *'household expenditure'*, meaning money spent. But the passage says the survey was about time spent — *'seven hours a day on transporting themselves and their goods'*. ***The survey was about time, not money***, so the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: Interesting facts regarding transport were found: 95% was on foot; 80% was within the locality; and 70% was related to the collection of water and firewood and travelling to grinding mills.

Q34: The question says *'one-fifth or 20%'* of transport was outside the local area. The passage states that *'80% was within the locality'*, which means the remaining 20% was outside. **80% inside** means **20% outside**, so the answer is **YES**.

items.sentence_raw: Having determined the main transport needs, possible solutions were identified which might reduce the time and burden.
During Phase II, from January to February 1991, a number of approaches were implemented in an effort to improve mobility and access to transport.
items.explain:
Q28: This section describes the first actions taken, like improving roads and introducing donkeys and wheelbarrows. The passage says *'a number of approaches were implemented'* to *'improve mobility and access'*. These are the **initial improvements** in how people moved, matching heading **v**.

Q31: The question says there were **'five phases'**, but the passage only lists *'Phase I'*, *'Phase II'*, and *'Phase III'*. ***Five is not three***, so the number in the statement is wrong. The text clearly names just these **three** stages of work. Therefore, the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: An improvement of the road network was considered necessary to ensure the import and export of goods to the district.
These improvements were carried out using methods that were heavily dependent on labour.
In addition to the improvement of roads, these methods provided training in the operation of a mechanical workshop and bus and truck services.
However, the difference from the conventional approach was that this time consideration was given to local transport needs outside the road network.
items.explain: Q28: This section describes the first actions taken, like improving roads and introducing donkeys and wheelbarrows. The passage says *'a number of approaches were implemented'* to *'improve mobility and access'*. These are the **initial improvements** in how people moved, matching heading **v**.

items.sentence_raw: Most goods were transported along the paths that provide short-cuts up and down the hillsides, but the paths were a real safety risk and made the journey on foot even more arduous.
It made sense to improve the paths by building steps, handrails and footbridges.
items.explain: Q36: The passage directly states it *'made sense to improve the paths by building steps, handrails and footbridges'*. These constructions were for paths on hillsides, which matches ending **D**: *'improved paths used for transport up and down hillsides'*.

items.sentence_raw: It was uncommon to find means of transport that were more efficient than walking but less technologically advanced than motor vehicles.
The use of bicycles was constrained by their high cost and the lack of available spare parts.
Oxen were not used at all but donkeys were used by a few households in the northern part of the district.
MIRTP focused on what would be most appropriate for the inhabitants of Makete in terms of what was available, how much they could afford and what they were willing to accept.
After careful consideration, the project chose the promotion of donkeys - a donkey costs less than a bicycle - and the introduction of a locally manufacturable wheelbarrow.

items.sentence_raw: At the end of Phase II, it was clear that the selected approaches to Makete's transport problems had had different degrees of success.
Phase III from March 1991 to March 1993, focused on the refinement and institutionalisation of these activities.

The text clearly names just these **three** stages of work. Therefore, the answer is **NO**.

items.sentence_raw: The road improvements and accompanying maintenance system had helped make the district centre accessible throughout the year.
Essential goods from outside the district had become more readily available at the market, and prices did not fluctuate as much as they had done before.
Paths and secondary roads were improved only at the request of communities who were willing to participate in construction and maintenance.
items.explain: Q38: The passage says that *'Paths and secondary roads were improved only at the request of communities who were willing to participate'*. **'Willing to participate'** means they were **'willing to lend a hand'**, so the correct ending is **G**.

items.sentence_raw: However, the improved paths impressed the inhabitants, and requests for assistance greatly increased soon after only a few improvements had been completed.

The efforts to improve the efficiency of the existing transport services were not very successful because most of the motorised vehicles in the district broke down and there were no resources to repair them.
items.explain: Q37: The passage explains that efforts to improve transport services failed because *'most of the motorised vehicles... broke down and there were no resources to repair them'*. This frequent breakdown of buses and trucks directly **hindered** attempts to make services better, matching ending **I**.

items.sentence_raw: Even the introduction of low-cost means of transport was difficult because of the general poverty of the district.
The locally manufactured wheelbarrows were still too expensive for all but a few of the households.
Modifications to the original design by local carpenters cut production time and costs.
Other local carpenters have been trained in the new design so that they can respond to requests.

Nevertheless, a locally produced wooden wheelbarrow which costs around 5000Tanzanian shillings (less than US $20) in Makete, and is about one quarter the cost of a metal wheelbarrow, is still too expensive for most people.
Donkeys, which were imported to the district, have become more common and contribute, in particular, to the transportation of crops and goods to market.
Those who have bought donkeys are mainly from richer households but, with an increased supply through local breeding, donkeys should become more affordable.
Meanwhile, local initiatives are promoting the renting out of the existing donkeys.
It should be noted, however, that a donkey, which at 20,000 Tanzanian shillings costs less than a bicycle, is still an investment equal to an average household's income over half a year.
This clearly illustrates the need for supplementary measures if one wants to assist the rural poor.

It would have been easy to criticise the MIRTP for using in the early phases a 'top-down' approach, in which decisions were made by experts and officials before being handed down to communities, but it was necessary to start the process from the level of the governmental authorities of the district.
items.explain: Q29: The passage explains that starting from the *'level of the governmental authorities'* was necessary, even if it seemed like a *'top-down'* approach. It says responding to villagers was difficult *'without the support and understanding of district authorities'*. This shows the **co-operation of district officials**, which is heading **x**.

items.sentence_raw: It would have been difficult to respond to the requests of villagers and other rural inhabitants without the support and understanding of district authorities.

items.sentence_raw: Today, nobody in the district argues about the importance of improved paths and inexpensive means of transport.
But this is the result of dedicated work over a long period, particularly from the officers in charge of community development.
They played an essential role in raising awareness and interest among the rural communities.
The concept of integrated rural transport is now well established in Tanzania, where a major program of rural transport is just about to start.
items.explain: Q30: The final section looks ahead, saying Makete's *'experiences... will help in this initiative'* and the district will be a *'reference for future work'*. This means MIRTP is being used as a **future model**, so the heading is **i**.
